title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is the front of an airmail envelope sent to 'Professeur Alexandre Grothendieck, 34700 Villecun (Lodève), FRANCE'. It carries a Nagoya University Faculty of Science postage-meter mark dated 20.12.77 (名古屋大学内 / NAGOYA DAIGAKUNAI, 0,340 yen, meter H1208) and a 'PAR AVION / 航空郵便' cachet. The red and blue airmail border and the 'VIA AIR MAIL / PAR AVION' lettering are hand-drawn. Faint mirror-image text shows through from the back. It is the sender's return address, already transcribed on the previous page: 'Jun-Ichi Yamashita c/o Mr. Mizuno, 43 Myoken-chō, Showa-ku, Nagoya 466, JAPAN'. So the letter came from Jun-Ichi Yamashita in Nagoya in December 1977. The envelope was later reused as scrap paper. Several lines of small marks in a shorthand-like script were added; in context they are probably Grothendieck's own jottings, made when the envelope was filed among the 1983–84 conformal-surgery notes. These marks are not legible to me, and I cannot claim any mathematical content for them. The pencil '13' is the archive page number; the pencil '340' (possibly '3X0') probably echoes the postage value. The neighbouring page (12) carries mathematics on the reverse: a chain of equivalences between an elliptic curve with a closed geodesic, a primitive rank-1 subgroup of π1, Tate-curve data, and a loxodromic automorphism of P^1. That content belongs to page 12, not to this page.

ideas.what: Provenance: a 1977 letter from Jun-Ichi Yamashita (Nagoya) to Grothendieck at Villecun, with the envelope reused as scratch paper in the 1983–84 conformal-surgery notes

missed.claim: The shorthand-like marks on the envelope are undeciphered. If they are Grothendieck's private shorthand, a palaeographic study could recover short notes accompanying the conformal-surgery material. Nothing mathematical can be asserted from the image itself.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of archival or biographical interest unless deciphered. It documents Grothendieck's Japanese correspondent in 1977 and his habit of reusing envelopes for notes.

deep.surprise_reason: An envelope with postal marks and illegible shorthand jottings; no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: The show-through mirror text in the upper middle is the sender's return address from the reverse ('Jun-Ichi Yamashita c/o Mr. Mizuno, 43 Myoken-chō, Showa-ku, Nagoya 466, JAPAN'), matching the line transcribed on the previous page.
The pencil number near the bottom may read '3X0' rather than '340'; it likely refers to the 340-yen postage.
The 'VIA AIR MAIL / PAR AVION' lettering and the red/blue border are hand-drawn, not a printed airmail envelope.
